properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 7 at 11:00AM AKDT until August 8 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Yentna River including Lake Creek.

* WHEN...Until 100 PM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1053 AM AKDT, the river remains in moderate flood stage
after heavy rains earlier this week, but is beginning to
subside. The river crested at 22.52 ft around 8pm Thursday,
August 7th.
- For Yentna River at Lake Creek:
At 9:50am the stage was 22.3 feet.
Flood Stage is 20.5 feet.

Impacts:
At 20.5 feet: Anglers Inn & King Point Lodges will have water
in several cabins.



At 22.0 feet: McDougal's, King Point, Anglers Inn, Wilderness
Place, Lake Creek Lodge, 3-Rivers, and Cottonwood Resorts
will have water in a number of cabins with water also
encroaching the main lodge buildings.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 7 at 9:46PM EDT until August 8 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Indianapolis IN
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northwestern Madison County in central Indiana...
East Central Tipton County in central Indiana...

* WHEN...Until 200 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 946 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the warned area. Between 1.5 and 2.5 inches of
rain have fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
mainly rural areas of Northwestern Madison and East Central
Tipton Counties
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 7 at 8:14PM CDT until August 8 at 9:48PM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Tilden...Minor flooding is forecast.

- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 15.2 feet
just after midnight tonight. It will then fall below flood stage
late tonight.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 15.2
feet on 09/19/1983.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 7 at 11:27PM EDT until August 8 at 5:30AM EDT by NWS Charleston WV
properties.description:

expected.

* WHERE...Southern Roane County in central West Virginia...
South Central Calhoun County in north central West Virginia...

* WHEN...Until 530 AM EDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Streams continue to rise due to excess runoff from
earlier rainfall. Expect many areas of slow moving or standing
water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1127 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly
in the warned area. Between 1.5 and 3 inches of rain have fallen.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Amma, Looneyville, Left Hand, Tariff and Walton.
- This includes Interstate 79 between mile markers 23 and 33.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Report flooding to the National Weather Service by calling toll free,

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 7 at 11:37PM CDT until August 8 at 3:00AM CDT by NWS Springfield MO
properties.description:
At 1137 PM CDT, Department of Transportations reported flooding was
occurring from thunderstorms that produced heavy rain across the
warned area this evening. Between 2 and 5 inches of rain have
fallen. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mountain View, Willow Springs and Ozark National Scenic Riverways.

Highway 17 was reported to be closed due to flooding at Jam Up Creek.

This includes the following low water crossings...
Eleven Point River at County Road 1550, Gill Branch at Highway Y
and Elevin Point River at Highway U.

properties.description:
FFWTWC

The National Weather Service in Tucson has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northwestern Cochise County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until midnight MST.

* At 912 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing 1 to
2 inches of heavy rain across the western portions of the Galiuro
Mountains. The heaviest rainfall has occurred across and near Hot
Springs Canyon. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly, especially along drainages through Hot Springs Canyon, as
well as Teran and Palomas Washes that drain into the San Pedro
River from the east.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Muleshoe Ranch Preserve and Cascabel.
